audits.text:
## fe4e4cc0157f

**Classification: reproduced generator-contract defect; left unchanged.** Generator SHA-256 `bf01cafd903b1cbb93bf0ad519045d2e703024c1b23e762a8fb9a1d463d20f61`; executed canonical rule hash `f2ec9c60993e`.

The advertised `texture` domain includes `all_solid`, but `generate(seed=431, sample_index=7, difficulty="medium", texture="all_solid")` returns three zero-hole objects and its own `self_check` rejects the result: `object hole counts must be distinct, got [0, 0, 0]` and `at least one object must have an interior hole`. Thus this value is not in the documented normal generator domain even though `AXES["texture"]["valid"]` says it is. The canonical Racket rule still executes and selects the largest solid rectangle, so the issue is the ordinary-axis contract, not rule execution.

Evidence: `checks/audit/fe4e4cc0157f/probe.json`, `checks/audit/fe4e4cc0157f/input.json`, and supported Racket receipt `checks/audit/fe4e4cc0157f/racket.json` (input SHA-256 `ed129305434d0b3569864606197646ab12e27e975af25eb6e3406db6a2197e64`). Recommended future repair: remove negative fixtures from the valid domain or explicitly classify them outside production generation.
